title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is the combinatorial type (a stable graph) of a stable marked curve X_G. A is the set of nodes (edges) and I the set of marked points (open half-edges); Â = A ⊔ I. The previous page builds X_G from its normalisation (a disjoint union of spheres Σ_{Â_s}) using the involution σ on half-edges. For each x ∈ Â it attaches a canonical U-torsor T_x, where U is the unit circle:
- for a marked point x over a component s, T_x is the circle of real tangent directions at x;
- for a node x, T_x is the circle of directions in the tensor product of the two branch tangent lines.
In both cases T_x is canonically induced from an explicit 2-element set ({±1}-torsor) via the inclusion {±1} ⊂ U.

This page.
1. Taking the product gives P_G = ∏_x T_x = U^Â ∧_{{±1}^Â} Sε_G. Here Sε_G = ∏_a ε_a is a torsor under {±1}^Â. The sign torsors are:
   - ε_a = Â_s \ {a} for a ∈ I (via the diametral-point bijection of the previous page);
   - ε_a = ∧_{ã over a} (Â_{σ(ã)} \ ã) for a ∈ A.
   So P_G (written SP_G) is a real torus torsor, with π_1 = Z^Â.
2. Plumbing/collar map. With smoothing moduli in ]0,1[ (one per node; the index set is written \vec A), one gets a canonical, up-to-homotopy map μ°×SP_G → PM_{G⇆}. The target is the moduli space of the nearby smoothed curves with tangential/rigidifying data. Modulus gives the node opening and phase gives the twist. Geometrically this is the collar of the stratum of type G in the real oriented blow-up (Harvey/Kato–Nakayama-type bordification); its fibre is the torus P_G.
3. On fundamental groups this gives Z^Â → ST_{G⇆}: Dehn twists about the vanishing cycles, plus full rotations at marked points. Better, it gives a morphism of fundamental groupoids.
4. The discrete set Sε_G (real directions) sits inside SP_G. Since μ° is simply connected (contractible), each ξ ∈ Sε_G determines an object of ST_{G⇆}, i.e. a 'base point at infinity' (tangential base point) attached to the degeneration G with a choice of real signs.
5. Define S_0T_G as the full subgroupoid of Π_1(P_G) on Sε_G. This gives a functor S_0T_G → ST_{G⇆}.

The next page presents S_0T_G by half-twist generators u_{α,ξ} (paths exp(πit)) with a Z^Â-valued cocycle n(α,β). Purpose: build the discrete 'Lego' of the Teichmüller tower, i.e. groupoids with base points at infinity at degenerate curves, glued from local pieces (as in Esquisse §3).
errors: Cardinality slip: Sε_G = ∏_{a∈Â} ε_a has cardinality 2^{card Â}, not 2^{card A} as written (unless the ε_a for a ∈ I are being disregarded, which the formula does not say).

The plumbing map μ°×SP_G → PM is called 'canonique', but it depends on local coordinate choices. It is canonical only up to contractible choice/homotopy, which is enough for the groupoid-level conclusions drawn.
Index set of μ°: written (]0,1[)^{\vec A}. Smoothing parameters should be one per node (indexed by A); if \vec A means oriented edges, the count doubles. Probably notational.
Notation drifts between P_G, SP_G and Π_1(P_G); harmless.

ideas.what: Torus torsor of tangent directions at nodes/marked points as the fibre over a boundary stratum, induced from a {±1}-torsor of real directions
ideas.modern_name: Fibre of the Kato–Nakayama space / real oriented blow-up of M̄_{g,n} along the boundary stratum; tangential directions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Harvey (bordification, 1974); Kato–Nakayama (1999); Looijenga; Deligne for tangential base points (1989)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to base points at infinity and the Teichmüller tower but without these formulas

ideas.what: Plumbing/collar map μ°×SP_G → PM_{G⇆} inducing Z^Â → Teichmüller group(oid) (Dehn twists along vanishing cycles)
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing coordinates / local monodromy of the stratum; Dehn twist subgroup of a multicurve

ideas.what: Discrete set Sε_G of 'real' tangential base points at infinity and the subgroupoid S_0T_G mapping to the Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points at maximally/partially degenerate curves; groupoid with base points at infinity (Teichmüller Lego)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, sketch); Deligne (tangential base points); Ihara–Nakamura; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Bakalov–Kirillov; Moore–Seiberg
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 (idea of base points at infinity and the Lego), not this explicit construction

missed.claim: Explicit canonical description of the discrete tangential base points at a stratum of type G as a {±1}^Â-torsor Sε_G of real tangent directions, with ε_a built combinatorially from the stable graph (diametral points for marked points, tensor of sign torsors for nodes). The fundamental groupoid restricted to these points, S_0T_G, has half-twist generators and maps functorially to the Teichmüller groupoid of the smoothed type.
missed.quote: Désignons par S_0T_G le sousgroupoïde de ST_G = Π_1(P_G) induit sur Sε_G, on a donc S_0T_G → ST_{G⇆}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a sign-refined, half-twist version of the tangential base-point formalism used in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory (HLS, Nakamura–Schneps). The ±1 real-direction choices and half-twists match the ribbon/half-twist data in modular-functor (Bakalov–Kirillov) presentations. It is a precise early formulation, and the literature does not seem to credit Grothendieck with it beyond the Esquisse sketch.

missed.claim: The 'S' construction (SP_G, SPM) anticipates the Kato–Nakayama / real oriented blow-up viewpoint on the boundary of moduli, with tangential base points as real points of the torus fibre.
missed.quote: μ°_{\vec A}×SP_G → PM_{G⇆} ... comme μ°_{\vec A} est simplt connexe ... Sε_G → Ob(ST_{G⇆})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links Grothendieck's Lego program to the log-geometric treatment of tangential base points developed only later.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, explicit construction of sign-torsor tangential base points and the groupoid S_0T_G, anticipating later formalisms (Deligne, HLS, Kato–Nakayama). The underlying ideas are known and partially sketched in the Esquisse, so this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a new result.

'(de cardinal 2^{card A})' is as written in the manuscript, but it should mathematically be 2^{card Â}.
'l'ensemble ε_G' should read 'l'ensemble Sε_G', consistent with the next line Sε_G ⊂ SP_G; the struck text before it reads roughly '∏ε_a = ∏ε_a ε_G'.
